question.text: How many back-to-back moves separate two tracks played at Lost Lands 2018, and how do we know each move happened? Does dsdk.worlds' answer, with its KNOWN/UNKNOWN verdict and witness path, agree with an independent oracle and an independent JS recomputation?

competing_explanations.name: correct
competing_explanations.description: The loader, graphs and search are right.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: 51 queries compared with an oracle script that shares no code and uses different algorithms; 40 random-world differential tests against dsdk.graph in pytest.

competing_explanations.name: inferred_edges_leak_into_known
competing_explanations.description: A path that needs a guessed (co-selected) step is reported as observed.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: Every KNOWN hop cites sets in which that exact transition occurs (analytic check); a mutant that ignores evidence is run and must disagree with the oracle.

competing_explanations.name: stale_or_altered_data
competing_explanations.description: The corpus differs from the one Sam's pipeline produced.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: The gzip's SHA-256 is pinned from jukebox's Pages workflow; a flipped bit is refused (deliberate failure).

competing_explanations.name: js_echoes_python
competing_explanations.description: The browser agrees only because it reads Python's numbers.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: The JS side decodes the embedded corpus and searches it itself; Python's answers are used only as the comparison column.

claims: For the 51 checked queries and 300 seeded random pairs, Python, the oracle (51) and JS agree on status, witness path, reason and per-step evidence.
KNOWN means every step was seen back-to-back in a cited DJ set; UNKNOWN means at least one step is only inferred from sharing a set, or no route exists in this sample.
The corpus is exactly the file whose SHA-256 is pinned in jukebox, with 1,352 tracks, 50 DJ credits, 54 sets and 1,919 transitions.
does_not_claim: That two tracks without a route are unrelated (open world, sampled corpus).
That the parser captured every set: 234 rows were rejected upstream.
That a DJ really intended a transition: only that the two tracks were adjacent in the recovered tracklist.
Anything about festivals other than Lost Lands 2018.

input_snapshot.source: jukebox derived store (public; no raw lines): samuelpmahan/jukebox@lab/composable-mining commit 8b4d32b44217f8b4eb08977c9920a03194b2b1b2, data/lostlands-2018.jukebox.json.gz reassembled from part00..part07 and vendored at fixtures/worlds/lostlands-2018.jukebox.json.gz.
input_snapshot.schema: jukebox-primitives/v1: artists[], tracks[[key,title,artists,featured,variation,variationArtists]], selectorGroups[[members,label,truncated]], dates[], selections[[track,group,date]], transitions[[source,target,group,date]]. Embedded verbatim in panels.world.
input_snapshot.missingness_meaning: A pair of tracks never seen together is NOT_OBSERVED (no edge is drawn). An edge from co-selection is UNKNOWN (inferred). A track id that is not in the corpus is INVALID. A date of -1 would mean 'undated' (none occur).

config.search: dsdk.graph.reachable for the verdict; shortest_path over observed edges, else candidate_path (fewest inferred edges, then hops, then node order)
config.graphs: transition (directed, weight=count, KNOWN), co-selection (undirected, UNKNOWN), search = observed + both directions of every co-selection

analytic.name: transition_weights_sum_to_transition_rows
analytic.description: Every observed transition row is counted exactly once in the edge weights.

analytic.name: search_edges_arithmetic
analytic.description: Six-degrees edges = 2 x co-selected pairs + observed edges that are not co-selected pairs (self-loops). Hand-derived from the two graph builders.

analytic.name: known_hops_are_real_transitions
analytic.description: Every KNOWN hop of every checked query appears as consecutive tracks in a set it cites.

independent_reference.description: fixtures/worlds/gen_slices.py recomputes paths with level-synchronous BFS and Bellman-Ford plus a backward distance table (the library uses a FIFO queue and Dijkstra); the browser adds a third implementation in viewer/w1.mjs.

comparisons.name: 51 six-degrees queries: status, reason, witness path, per-step evidence vs gen_slices.py (independent algorithms)

boundary_cases.name: invalid_node_is_not_unknown
boundary_cases.description: A track id outside the corpus is INVALID (a different answer from UNKNOWN).

boundary_cases.name: no_path_is_unknown_not_known_false
boundary_cases.description: Disconnected pair in an open world: UNKNOWN (never KNOWN False).

boundary_cases.name: weak_components
boundary_cases.description: The transition graph has 5 weak components (one giant of 1,276 tracks); the search graph has the same 5.

deliberate_failures.name: naive_search_over_all_edges
deliberate_failures.description: MUTANT: breadth-first over every edge and call the result KNOWN. It must disagree with the oracle on queries whose best path needs an inferred step.
deliberate_failures.detail: 7 of 7 inferred-path queries would be reported KNOWN by the mutant

deliberate_failures.name: tampered_corpus_bytes
deliberate_failures.description: Flip one bit of the vendored gzip: the loader must refuse it before decoding.

run_record.random_draws: 300 track pairs drawn with random.Random(2018).randrange for the 'How far apart?' view; the JS side replays the same pairs from the packet.
run_record.uncertainty: Path answers are exact for this corpus (no sampling). The corpus is a SAMPLE of one festival: 234 source rows were rejected by the parser, two credits are truncated ('+ More'), and the parser strips leading digits from artist names (12th Planet appears as 'th Planet' on 8 tracks). 'No route' therefore never means 'impossible'.

accessibility: labelled search inputs with a suggestion list; the path is an ordered list
status is a word (KNOWN / UNKNOWN / INVALID), never colour alone
every table has a caption and header cells

result.statement: On the pinned Lost Lands 2018 corpus, 51 checked queries and 300 seeded random pairs give the same verdict, witness path and step evidence in Python, the independent oracle and the browser. Of the random pairs 243 are connected by observed steps alone (median 10 hops, longest 36), 35 need an inferred step and 22 have no route in this sample. The mutant that ignores evidence is caught.
result.next_bounded_experiment: Remove the 169-track truncated credit ('Excision & Sullivan King & Dion Timmer + More', 2018-09-13) and recompute the distance histogram: how many pairs lose their short route? Then repeat with the sets weighted by 1/size so a huge set stops dominating co-selection.
